submitted.rationale: Index 0 (Bi0.97Sb0.03) gave the highest measured EQE (3.1e-4 %). It is near α-Bi2O3, which MACE puts on the hull (stable) and MEGNet predicts has a gap of about 2.34 eV, below the 2.4 eV photon energy. The other two measured regions gave near-zero EQE.

rejected.reason: Measured EQE 8.7e-5 %. Near sillenite Bi12SbO20 (predicted gap 1.68 eV) but performed poorly.
Measured EQE of about zero (-4.7e-5 %). Near Bi3SbO7.
MEGNet HSE gap 3.06 eV, so it cannot absorb 2.4 eV photons; not measured.

consultations.verdict: Support: MEGNet HSE gaps show Bi-rich phases (Bi12SbO20 1.68 eV, Bi3SbO7 2.27, Bi2O3 2.34) absorb 2.4 eV photons while BiSbO4 (3.06) does not. Index 5 (Sb 0.0745) matches sillenite Bi12SbO20 stoichiometry, lowest gap.
Support: MACE puts Bi3SbO7 on the hull (0 eV/atom), so it should form at index 14 (Sb 0.249). With its 2.27 eV gap it absorbs 2.4 eV light. Index 5 (sillenite region) gave negligible EQE.

Weak support: MACE puts α-Bi2O3 on the hull, and its predicted gap of 2.34 eV absorbs 2.4 eV light. Index 0, the most Bi-rich candidate, should be mostly Bi2O3. The sillenite and Bi3SbO7 regions both measured about zero, so the unexplored Bi-rich end is the remaining untested region that absorbs at this energy.
